First of all, this was a FOUR engine aircraft. The B-17 was a rugged motherfucker that was known to make it back from bombing missions with three of the four engines knocked out and huge gaping holes blown in the fuselage by flack...they don't go down easily. This one took off and suddenly started losing power, witnesses said all four engines were sputtering and belching smoke. The plane tried to turn around and do an emergency landing, but apparently lost all power coming in and crashed on the runway.

The odd thing, and one of the first things I noticed, was the thick plume of black smoke that rose from the burning wreckage.

B-17s burn gasoline...high octane aviation fuel, whereas jets burn "Jet A", which is essentially kerosene/diesel. There's a HUGE difference as to how these fuels burn in a crash; gasoline goes up in a fireball and burns off relatively quickly, jet fuel burns slowly, and produces huge amounts of thick black smoke.

That B-17 had the wrong type of fuel in it. You don't have to take my word for this, ask ANYONE who knows about aircraft (or firefighting for that matter) and they'll tell you the same thing...someone fueled up this aircraft with jet fuel, either by mistake, or intentionally. I'm guessing there was probably enough gas in the lines to start the engines and get off the ground, but as soon as the "Jet A" got sucked into the engines they conked out. I've personally seen gasoline-powered cars that someone accidentally filled with diesel, and that's exactly how they react...they start up just fine, and a few miles down the road they begin sputtering and smoking before they conk out.

If the NTSB comes up with any other explanation for this crash other than the fuel, they're lying, and that's why I'm anxiously awaiting the results of the investigation. Yeah, the fuel mix-up COULD have been an accident, but airport re-fuelers are VERY careful about things like this not happening.
